answer: A vault-backed stake bond is the simplest durable filter: to earn, an agent locks a deposit in a time-locked vault for thirty days, and any proven misbehaviour slashes it. The bond alone is not enough, so every claim must echo through at least three independent verifiers who stake their own deposits on its truth; a false echo costs them too. Reputation then grows like a juniper, slowly, so a fresh identity starts near zero and cannot buy history. An attacker spawning a thousand identities must fund a thousand vaults and risk slashing on every lie, turning a cheap flood into an expensive siege.
